name: Requirements Gathering & Documentation
one_line_goal: Turn the feature wish-list into a precise, testable specification that nobody has to guess at later.
objective: Produce a complete, unambiguous Product Requirements Document before writing any code, and surface every ambiguity as an explicit question rather than a silent assumption.
rationale: Every requirement in this brief touches money movement. An ambiguity that survives into the schema costs a migration and a data-correctness incident later. This stage exists to make the expensive questions cheap.
entry_criteria: 00_project_manifest.json has been read in full, including the invariants and the open questions register.
The user is available to answer clarifying questions before Stage 2 begins.

how_to_work_this_stage.unit_of_work: One substage per working session. Work them strictly in listed order; do not parallelise or skip.
how_to_work_this_stage.between_substages: Tick the substage off, append evidence to docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then start the next. No user approval needed between substages.
how_to_work_this_stage.at_stage_end: The final substage assembles the stage report and stops for user approval before the next stage file is opened.
substage_list: 1.4 The money model in plain language
1.6 Scope boundaries and the version 1 cut line

substages.name: Intake and source reconciliation
substages.goal: Inventory every stated requirement from the source brief so nothing can be quietly dropped later.
substages.why_it_matters: The most common requirements failure is not misinterpretation, it is omission. Building the inventory first makes omission detectable.
entry_criteria: 00_project_manifest.json has been read in full, including the invariants and the open questions register.
The user is available to answer clarifying questions before Stage 2 begins.

work.action: Extract every distinct requirement statement from the manifest into a flat working list, one line each, preserving the original wording verbatim alongside its FR or NFR id.
details: Do not paraphrase at this point - paraphrasing is where requirements quietly change meaning.
Include requirements that are implied by the predefined_categories and cloud_sync_requirements blocks, not only those in the FR list.
Note that the manifest lists 15 FRs and 8 NFRs; if your inventory has a different count, reconcile before continuing.

work.action: Split any compound requirement that contains more than one testable claim into separate sub-requirements, keeping the parent id and adding a letter suffix.
details: Example: FR-04 covers both logging an income event and auto-splitting it; those are two verifiable behaviours and become FR-04a and FR-04b.
Example: FR-14 covers monthly summaries, yearly summaries, category trends and CSV export - four distinct capabilities.

work.action: Classify each requirement: functional, non-functional, constraint, or assumption presented as a requirement.
details: A constraint is something the design must not do, such as never using a third-party server.
An assumption presented as a requirement is a red flag - route it to substage 1.7.

work.action: Identify the requirements that touch money movement and mark them as CRITICAL, because they will need failure-case acceptance criteria in substage 1.3.
Cross-check the inventory against the global invariants INV-01 to INV-12 and flag any requirement that appears to conflict with one.
details: A conflict here is a genuine finding and must be escalated, not resolved silently.

work.action: Write the inventory into docs/PRD.md as an appendix table so the final document carries its own provenance.

acceptance_criteria: Every FR and NFR id from the manifest appears in the inventory exactly once, with its verbatim source wording.
Every compound requirement has been split, and the split is justified in one line each.
Requirements touching money movement are marked CRITICAL and counted.
Any requirement conflicting with an invariant is listed separately and escalated rather than resolved.
outputs: docs/PRD.md appendix: source requirement inventory table.
must_not: Do not paraphrase source wording in this substage.
Do not resolve conflicts you discover - record and escalate them.
common_pitfalls: Collapsing two requirements into one because they appear in the same sentence.
Treating the predefined category list as decorative rather than as a requirement with real implications for onboarding.
definition_of_done: The inventory is complete, counted, and cross-checked against the invariants.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 1.2. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: An open question (OQ-xx) blocks the work in front of you.
A global invariant (INV-xx) cannot be satisfied as designed.
This substage reveals that an earlier approved stage is wrong.

substages.name: Personas and end-to-end journeys
substages.goal: Describe who uses the app and the exact step-by-step paths they take, including the paths where things go wrong.
substages.why_it_matters: Stage 2 derives the navigation graph directly from these journeys. A missing journey becomes a missing screen.
entry_criteria: Substage 1.1 (Intake and source reconciliation) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Expand persona P1, the personal saver: goals, financial context, technical confidence, device assumptions, what triggers them to open the app, and what would make them abandon it.
details: Be concrete about context of use: often on a phone, often distracted, often within minutes of receiving money.
State their prior budgeting experience as none, because NFR-04 depends on that assumption.

work.action: Expand persona P2, the owner-operator: the same, plus the business pressures that make mixing business and personal money costly for them.
details: Capture why separation matters emotionally, not only structurally - business float spent on groceries is the failure they fear.

work.action: Write the P1 primary journey as numbered steps, naming a screen at every step.
details: First launch, currency confirmation, choosing scope, setting top-level ratios, accepting suggested categories, setting within-group percentages, optionally setting ceilings, optionally adding accounts, landing on the dashboard.
Then: logging the first salary, previewing the split, confirming, seeing the result.
Then: logging a grocery spend and checking the dashboard the next day.

work.action: Write the P2 primary journey, covering business setup and a business income event that hits an inventory ceiling and overflows.
details: The overflow moment is the single most important thing to get right in the design; describe what the user should understand at that moment.

work.action: Write at least five failure journeys, each ending with the user still in control of their data.
details: No internet on first launch, all the way through onboarding and a first income event.
Google permission revoked later, discovered on the next sync attempt.
A mistaken income entry that must be undone.
A second device added months later, needing to receive existing history.
The user's phone is lost and they install on a replacement device.

work.action: For every journey, mark the step with the highest abandonment risk and state in one sentence what the design must do at that step.
Estimate the wall-clock time for the P1 setup journey when every default is accepted, and record the target of under 5 minutes from NFR-04.

acceptance_criteria: Both primary journeys are written as numbered steps with a named screen at each step.
At least five failure journeys exist and none ends in a dead end or in data loss.
Every journey names its highest-risk step and the design response.
The P1 default-accepting setup path is short enough to plausibly complete in under 5 minutes, and the step count supports that claim.
must_not: Do not design screens here - name them and describe what the user does, not how the screen looks.
Do not invent a third persona without raising it as a scope question.
common_pitfalls: Writing only happy-path journeys, which produces a design with no error states.
Journeys written at a level so abstract that no screen can be derived from them.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 1.3. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: An open question (OQ-xx) blocks the work in front of you.
A global invariant (INV-xx) cannot be satisfied as designed.
This substage reveals that an earlier approved stage is wrong.

substages.name: User stories and acceptance criteria
substages.goal: Convert every inventoried requirement into a user story with observable Given/When/Then criteria.
substages.why_it_matters: A wish-list item is not testable. A story with criteria is what Stage 9 verifies against.
substages.estimated_session: The longest substage of this stage. Expect it to take a full session.
entry_criteria: Substage 1.2 (Personas and end-to-end journeys) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: For every inventoried requirement, write one or more stories in the form: As a <P1 or P2>, I want <capability>, so that <outcome>.
details: Give each story a stable id US-001 onward and record the FR or NFR id it satisfies.
Where a requirement serves both personas differently, write two stories rather than one vague one.

work.action: Attach Given/When/Then acceptance criteria to every story, observable from outside the app.
details: No criterion may reference an internal class, table or function.
Each criterion must be checkable by a person holding a phone.

work.action: For every story marked CRITICAL in 1.1, add at least one negative or failure criterion.
details: For income splitting: what happens at zero, at one minor unit, at a very large amount, and when the percentages are stale.
For ceilings: what the user sees when a category is already full before the income arrives.
For overrides: what happens when the overridden amounts do not total the income.

work.action: Write the interaction stories explicitly, because FR-10, FR-11 and FR-12 interact and the interaction is where defects live.
details: A manual override that pushes a category past its ceiling - state the expected behaviour.
A fixed-recurring category that is already funded for the period when new income arrives.
A redirect target that is itself full - state what the user should see.
A redirect chain that ends at the sink - state how it is explained.

work.action: Assign MoSCoW priority to each story, inheriting the manifest FR priority unless there is a reason to differ, and state the reason where you differ.
Flag every story whose criteria you could not write without guessing, and carry the guess to substage 1.7 as an open question.
Build the FR-to-story coverage table and confirm no FR is uncovered.

acceptance_criteria: Every FR id is covered by at least one story; the coverage table shows no gaps.
No story contains the words etc, and so on, appropriate, or as needed.
Every story has at least one Given/When/Then criterion.
Every CRITICAL story has at least one negative or failure criterion.
The four interaction cases between ceilings, fixed-recurring categories and overrides each have an explicit expected behaviour.
outputs: docs/PRD.md section 5: functional requirements as user stories.
docs/PRD.md coverage table: FR id to story ids.
must_not: Do not write criteria that presuppose an implementation.
Do not skip the negative cases for money-moving stories - they are the point.
common_pitfalls: Acceptance criteria that restate the story in different words without adding a check.
Leaving the ceiling-plus-override interaction undefined, which forces the Stage 5 implementer to invent policy.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 1.4. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: An open question (OQ-xx) blocks the work in front of you.
A global invariant (INV-xx) cannot be satisfied as designed.
This substage reveals that an earlier approved stage is wrong.

substages.name: The money model in plain language
substages.goal: Define what a balance, a ceiling, a redirect and a category type mean in words a non-developer can act on.
substages.why_it_matters: Stage 2 designs the schema straight from this section. Loose words here produce a loose schema.
entry_criteria: Substage 1.3 (User stories and acceptance criteria) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: Manifest domain glossary and global invariants.

work.action: Define what a category balance means, and just as importantly what it does not mean.
details: It is money set aside and not yet spent, as recorded in the app.
It is not necessarily what any bank shows, because the app has no bank connection.
State that it is always derived from recorded events, never typed in directly (INV-04).

work.action: Define each category type, what full means for it, and what happens on overflow.
details: ACCUMULATING_RESERVE: grows toward a ceiling; overflow redirects.
FIXED_RECURRING: funded up to a known bill amount per period; surplus redirects rather than accumulating.
UNCAPPED_FLOW if OQ-03 is resolved in favour: a spending envelope with no cap and therefore no overflow.
State plainly for each type whether spending from it reopens headroom.

work.action: Define a ceiling as a target for accumulation, and state explicitly that it is not a spending limit.
details: This distinction confuses users of other budgeting apps and must be unambiguous in the product language.

work.action: Define the relationship between categories and bank accounts, resolving OQ-02 or presenting both options with their consequences.
details: Option A: accounts are informational labels with a derived total.
Option B: accounts hold real balances requiring transfers and reconciliation, which is materially more scope.

work.action: State the conservation rule in user terms.
details: Every unit of income lands in exactly one category, always.
The app will always be able to show the user where every unit went.
Nothing is ever rounded away or absorbed.

work.action: Describe redirect chains with a worked, human-readable example using real seeded category names and real figures.
details: Use a chain of at least three categories ending somewhere uncapped.
Show the arithmetic so a reader can verify conservation by hand.

work.action: Define the sink category concept in user language and state that it cannot be deleted, per OQ-07.
Define what a reversal is, per OQ-09: history is never edited, mistakes are corrected by an opposing entry that stays visible.

acceptance_criteria: A non-developer reading this section can correctly predict where money goes in a ceiling-overflow scenario.
At least one worked numeric example is included and its arithmetic conserves the input exactly.
Nothing in the section contradicts INV-01 through INV-12.
Each category type states its full condition, its overflow behaviour, and whether spending reopens headroom.
must_not: Do not introduce schema or column names.
Do not use percentages expressed as decimals - the product language should stay in whole percentages, with basis points reserved for the design.
common_pitfalls: Describing a ceiling in a way that a user reads as a spending cap.
Leaving the spending-reopens-headroom question implicit, which produces two incompatible reasonable implementations.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 1.5. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: An open question (OQ-xx) blocks the work in front of you.
A global invariant (INV-xx) cannot be satisfied as designed.
This substage reveals that an earlier approved stage is wrong.

substages.name: Non-functional requirements with measurable targets
substages.goal: Give every quality attribute a number or a binary observable condition, plus the stage that verifies it.
substages.why_it_matters: Fast and private are not requirements until they have a threshold and a test.
entry_criteria: Substage 1.4 (The money model in plain language) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: Journeys from 1.2 for data volume reasoning.

work.action: Restate NFR-01 to NFR-08 in the PRD and sharpen each measurable target where you can make it more specific.
Specify offline behaviour in detail.
details: Which operations must succeed with no network - the answer should be all of them.
What the UI shows when sync is stale, and what it shows for a user who never signs in.
How the user is told their data is device-only, without alarming them.

work.action: Specify sync expectations from the user's point of view, not the engineer's.
details: What they should see if they edited the same category on two devices.
What they should see after a month offline.
What they should never see: a spinner blocking the app, or data silently changing without explanation.

work.action: Specify privacy in language reusable as the basis of the Stage 10 privacy policy.
details: What leaves the device, what permissions are requested and why, what the developer can never see.
State the constraint that there is no developer-operated backend of any kind.

work.action: Specify performance budgets with numbers.
details: Cold start, dashboard render, allocation preview latency while typing, report generation, export duration.
Name the reference device class - a mid-tier phone, not a flagship.

work.action: Specify accessibility targets concretely: screen reader coverage, touch target size, contrast ratio, font scaling limit.
Derive data volume assumptions and state the five-year ledger size they imply.
details: Categories 10 to 40, income events 1 to 20 per month, spending transactions 30 to 200 per month.
Compute the resulting row counts, because Stage 2 sizes indexes from this and Stage 9 builds synthetic datasets from it.

work.action: For each NFR, name the stage and the artefact that will verify it.

acceptance_criteria: Every NFR has a number or a binary observable condition attached.
Every NFR names its verifying stage and artefact.
The data volume section produces concrete five-year row counts.
The privacy section is complete enough to draft a policy from without further research.
outputs: docs/PRD.md section 7: data volume and growth assumptions.
must_not: Do not write a target you have no intention of measuring.
Do not specify a performance target on a flagship device and call it representative.
common_pitfalls: Targets so loose they can never fail, which makes Stage 9 a formality.
Omitting the data volume section, which leaves Stage 2 unable to justify its indexes.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 1.6. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: An open question (OQ-xx) blocks the work in front of you.
A global invariant (INV-xx) cannot be satisfied as designed.

substages.name: Scope boundaries and the version 1 cut line
substages.goal: Name what is in, what is out, what is deferred, and which deferrals still need schema accommodation now.
substages.why_it_matters: The brief implies more than one release. Naming what is out prevents it being built by accident, and naming what must be accommodated prevents a migration later.
entry_criteria: Substage 1.5 (Non-functional requirements with measurable targets) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Restate the non-goals from the manifest and add any discovered during 1.1 to 1.5.
For each story, decide in-scope for version 1 or deferred, and justify every deferral in one line.
Produce the version 1 acceptance definition as a tick-list: the shortest set of capabilities that makes the app worth opening daily.
details: If a capability is not on this list, it is not blocking release.

work.action: For every deferred feature, classify it as schema-safe to defer, or requires schema accommodation now.
details: Name the accommodation explicitly where one is needed - for example the target_date column implied by OQ-04.
This classification is the single most valuable output of this substage.

work.action: Identify any scope creep risk implied by the business features and state the boundary that keeps this a budgeting app rather than accounting software (R-05).
Sanity-check the cut line against the journeys from 1.2: every step of both primary journeys must be supported by an in-scope capability.

acceptance_criteria: The version 1 cut line is a tick-list, not a paragraph.
Every deferral is labelled schema-safe or requires-accommodation, with the accommodation named where applicable.
Every step of both primary journeys is supported by an in-scope capability.
The boundary against accounting-software creep is stated in one sentence.
outputs: docs/PRD.md section 3: scope, deferrals and the version 1 cut line.
must_not: Do not defer anything that the primary journeys depend on.
Do not defer a feature that needs schema accommodation without naming the accommodation.
common_pitfalls: A cut line so generous that Stage 6 never ends.
Deferring a feature whose later addition would force a data migration, without saying so.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 1.7. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: An open question (OQ-xx) blocks the work in front of you.
A global invariant (INV-xx) cannot be satisfied as designed.
This substage reveals that an earlier approved stage is wrong.

substages.name: Open questions and ambiguity register
substages.goal: Collect every ambiguity into one register, each with options, consequences and a recommended default.
substages.why_it_matters: Unanswered questions are the real output of a requirements stage. Questions answered by silent assumption are how projects go wrong.
entry_criteria: Substage 1.6 (Scope boundaries and the version 1 cut line) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Carry all ten manifest open questions into docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md unchanged.
Add every ambiguity flagged during this stage, numbered from OQ-11 onward.
details: Candidate questions worth interrogating if not already raised: is income only salary or any inbound money including business revenue and refunds; does business revenue flow through the same three-way split or a business-only split; can one bank account hold several categories, and can one category span several accounts; what happens when a group has a non-zero percentage but no active categories; should spending from a savings category be possible at all or only a transfer out; is there a concept of a transfer between categories.

work.action: For each question record: the question in plain language, why it matters, which stage it blocks, the options with their consequences, and your recommended default.
details: The recommended default is what lets the user answer go with your defaults in a single message.

work.action: Split the register into BLOCKING - must be answered before Stage 2 - and NON-BLOCKING.
details: Be ruthless. A question is blocking only if design cannot proceed without it.

work.action: Write the blocking list as a short numbered list in plain language, free of technical jargon, ready to put in front of the user at the gate.
Record every non-blocking default as an assumption A-xx in docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md, with the impact if it turns out wrong and a review point.

acceptance_criteria: Every open question states a recommended default.
The blocking list is short enough to answer in a few minutes.
No question requires the user to understand Flutter, databases or sync to answer it.
Every non-blocking default appears as a numbered assumption with its impact-if-wrong stated.
must_not: Do not resolve a blocking question by assumption.
Do not pad the register with trivia that buries the important questions.
common_pitfalls: Phrasing a question so the user cannot answer without a design conversation.
Recording a default without stating what breaks if it is wrong.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_1_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 1.8. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.

substages.name: Traceability matrix and PRD assembly
substages.goal: Assemble the finished PRD, build the traceability matrix, and prepare the stage gate.
substages.why_it_matters: The matrix is the mechanism that stops a requirement quietly disappearing between Stage 1 and Stage 10.
entry_criteria: Substage 1.7 (Open questions and ambiguity register) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: All PRD sections drafted in 1.1 to 1.7.

work.action: Build docs/TRACEABILITY.md with columns: FR or NFR id, story ids, implementing stage or stages, verifying artefact, status.
details: Seed every status as NOT_STARTED; later stages update the same file rather than creating their own.

work.action: Verify the matrix has one row per manifest FR and NFR, with no empty implementing-stage cell.
Assemble docs/PRD.md in the required section order and read it end to end as a single document.
details: Sections: purpose and vision; personas and journeys; scope and cut line; money model; user stories; non-functional requirements; data volume; open questions; glossary; traceability reference; source inventory appendix.

work.action: Run a consistency pass across the whole PRD.
details: Terminology matches the manifest glossary exactly - no synonyms introduced.
No section contains implementation detail.
No requirement appears in one section and contradicts itself in another.
Every number stated in one place matches the same number stated elsewhere.

work.action: Run a completeness pass against the substage 1.1 inventory: every inventoried requirement appears somewhere in the finished PRD.
Write docs/reports/STAGE_1_REPORT.md using the manifest stage report sections.
details: Include the count of stories written, the coverage table result, and the blocking question list.

work.action: Prepare the gate message: deliverables, blocking questions in plain language, and the request to proceed.

acceptance_criteria: TRACEABILITY.md has exactly one row per manifest FR and NFR, none with an empty implementing stage.
The completeness pass shows every inventoried requirement present in the PRD.
The consistency pass finds no contradictory statements or introduced synonyms.
The stage report is complete and the gate question is drafted.
must_not: Do not proceed to Stage 2 before the user answers the blocking questions or explicitly authorises the defaults.
common_pitfalls: A traceability matrix built once and never updated, which is worse than none because it looks authoritative.
Assembling without reading end to end, which leaves contradictions between sections written on different days.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Final substage. Assemble the stage report, then STOP and request approval using approval_gate.question_to_user below.
escalate_immediately_if: The user has not answered the blocking questions.
The completeness pass finds a requirement with no home in the PRD.

stage_definition_of_done: PRD.md contains all required sections with no placeholder text.
Every manifest FR and NFR is traceable to at least one user story.
All open questions are registered, prioritised and carry a recommended default.
No section of the PRD contains implementation detail - no class names, table definitions or package choices.
The blocking questions have been put to the user in plain language.
stage_must_not: Do not write any application code.
Do not create UI mockups, wireframes or visual designs.
Do not define database schemas, table structures or column types.
Do not choose packages, libraries or a state management approach - that is Stage 2.
Do not resolve a blocking open question by assumption. Ask.
Do not silently expand scope beyond the brief; propose additions as open questions instead.
anti_patterns: Restating the feature list with different formatting and calling it a PRD.
Writing acceptance criteria that only an engineer could test.
Burying an ambiguity in a parenthetical instead of raising it.
Producing thirty open questions, most of them trivial, so the important three get lost.

artifacts_next_stage_consumes: PRD.md section on the money model drives the Stage 2 data model.
PRD.md journeys drive the Stage 2 navigation flow.
PRD.md NFR targets drive Stage 2 architecture trade-offs.
Answered open questions unblock Stage 2 design decisions.
handoff.summary_to_write: List the design constraints Stage 2 must honour, derived from this stage.

approval_gate.question_to_user: Stage 1 (Requirements) is complete. Deliverables: PRD.md, TRACEABILITY.md, ASSUMPTIONS.md, OPEN_QUESTIONS.md. I need answers to these blocking questions before design: <numbered list>. Do you approve moving to Stage 2?
